theme: The Viking Age: Raiders, Sagas & Norse Expansion
title: The Viking Age: Raiders, Sagas & Norse Expansion
description: A 60-question grand assessment on longships, Lindisfarne, Norse mythology, Danelaw, Vinland exploration, and heroic sagas.

questions.question: Which legendary monastery raid in Northumbria in 793 CE is commonly marked as the start of the Viking Age?
questions.explanation: The violent attack on the holy island monastery of Lindisfarne in June 793 sent shockwaves through Christian Europe.

questions.question: What was the specialized clinker-built warship that enabled Viking navigators to sail shallow rivers and open oceans?
questions.explanation: The Viking longship featured overlapping planks, a shallow draft, and symmetrical ends that allowed rapid beach landings.

questions.question: Who was the Norse explorer who led expeditions to Vinland in North America around 1000 CE?
questions.explanation: Leif Erikson established a settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in modern Newfoundland roughly 500 years before Columbus.

questions.question: What alphabetical writing system was carved onto Norse memorial stones and weapons?
questions.explanation: The Younger Futhark runic alphabet consisted of 16 characters used during the Viking Age for inscriptions and memorials.

questions.question: In Norse cosmology, what is the name of the great cosmic tree that connects the nine worlds?
questions.explanation: Yggdrasil is the sacred ash tree whose branches extend into the heavens and whose roots anchor the nine Norse realms.

questions.question: In what year CE did the historic Viking raid on the abbey of Lindisfarne take place?
questions.explanation: The raid on Lindisfarne in 793 CE is universally accepted as the formal dawn of the Viking Age.

questions.question: Which magnificent hall in Asgard, ruled by Odin, welcomed brave fallen warriors to feast for eternity?
questions.explanation: Valhalla welcomed warriors slain in battle (Einherjar), where they feasted on the boar Saehrimnir and prepared for Ragnarok.

questions.question: What fierce Viking warriors entered combat in a trance-like fury, wearing animal skins instead of armor?
questions.explanation: Berserkers were frenzied Norse champions associated with Odin who fought with ferocious abandon.

questions.question: Which Danish king ruled a vast North Sea Empire uniting England, Denmark, and Norway in the 11th century?
questions.explanation: King Cnut the Great forged an Anglo-Scandinavian empire from 1016 to 1035, bringing stability and trade to the region.

questions.question: What archaeological site in Newfoundland proves Norse presence in North America centuries before 1492?
questions.explanation: Excavated in the 1960s, L'Anse aux Meadows contains eight Norse turf-built structures and an iron smithy.

questions.question: What was the assembly or parliament called in medieval Scandinavia where free men made laws and resolved disputes?
questions.explanation: The Thing was the local legislative and judicial assembly, with Iceland Althing founded in 930 CE being one of the world oldest.

questions.question: In what year CE was the Althing, the national parliament of Iceland, founded at Thingvellir?
questions.explanation: The Icelandic Althing was established in 930 CE and remains one of the oldest surviving parliamentary institutions.

questions.question: Which elite imperial bodyguard unit served the Byzantine emperors in Constantinople, composed primarily of Norse warriors?
questions.explanation: The Varangian Guard was established under Basil II in 988 CE, celebrated for their two-handed Danish battleaxes.

questions.question: What was the Norse name for the Atlantic island of Greenland, named by Erik the Red to attract settlers?
questions.explanation: Erik the Red coined the appealing name Gronland (Greenland) in 982 CE to persuade fellow Icelanders to colonize the territory.

questions.question: Which god wielded the thunder hammer Mjolnir in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation: Thor, son of Odin and protector of mankind, used the short-handled war hammer Mjolnir to battle giants and control lightning.

questions.question: What major battle in 1066 in northern England saw King Harold Godwinson defeat King Harald Hardrada of Norway?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Stamford Bridge in September 1066 resulted in the death of Harald Hardrada and ended Norwegian invasion hopes.

questions.question: Which Norse term referred to the cataclysmic twilight and destruction of the gods and cosmos?
questions.explanation: Ragnarok involved cosmic battles, the death of Odin and Thor, and the eventual rebirth of the earth from the sea.

questions.question: In what year CE did the climactic Battle of Stamford Bridge take place, marking the traditional end of the Viking Age?
questions.explanation: 1066 CE saw the Battle of Stamford Bridge, which alongside the Norman Conquest concluded the Scandinavian Viking expansion era.

questions.question: What Norse navigation tool utilized light polarization to locate the sun on cloudy or overcast days?
questions.explanation: Iceland spar crystals, known in sagas as sunstones, polarized diffuse sunlight to determine solar coordinates.

questions.question: Which Viking leader was granted lands in northern France in 911 CE by King Charles the Simple, founding Normandy?
questions.explanation: Rollo signed the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte, converting to Christianity and becoming the first Duke of Normandy.

questions.question: What was the historical region of northern and eastern England governed by Scandinavian law called?
questions.explanation: The Danelaw was established by treaties between King Alfred the Great of Wessex and the Danish warlord Guthrum.

questions.question: Which female Norse deity of love, fertility, and gold rode a chariot pulled by two blue cats?
questions.explanation: Freyja was the foremost Vanir goddess who received half of all fallen warriors at her meadow Folkvangr.

questions.question: What famous 9th-century Viking ship burial uncovered in Norway is renowned for its elaborate wood carvings?
questions.explanation: The Oseberg ship, discovered near Tonsberg in 1904, contained the remains of two high-ranking women and rich textiles.

questions.question: Approximately how many oars were rowed on the magnificent Oseberg Viking longship?
questions.explanation: The Oseberg ship featured 15 oar holes on each side, requiring a rowing crew of 30 oarsmen plus steersman.

questions.question: Which legendary Viking king was said to have been killed in a pit of venomous vipers by King Aella of Northumbria?
questions.explanation: Ragnar Lothbrok legendary death spurred his sons to launch the Great Heathen Army against the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms in 865 CE.

questions.question: What precious silver wealth hoard was buried by Vikings in the 10th century and found in Lancashire in 1840?
questions.explanation: The Cuerdale Hoard contained over 8,600 silver items including Islamic dirhams, making it one of Europe largest Viking hoards.

questions.question: What primary trade route connected Scandinavian merchants with the Islamic Abbasid Caliphate via the Volga River?
questions.explanation: The Volga route linked the Baltic Sea to the Caspian Sea and Baghdad, trading furs, amber, and slaves for silver dirhams.

questions.question: Which mythological wolf offspring of Loki is destined to swallow Odin whole during Ragnarok?
questions.explanation: The colossal monstrous wolf Fenrir was bound with the magical silk ribbon Gleipnir until his escape at Ragnarok.

questions.question: Which King of Norway unified the separate petty kingdoms into a single Norwegian realm around 872 CE?
questions.explanation: Harald Fairhair won the decisive naval Battle of Hafrsfjord around 872 CE, becoming the first recognized King of Norway.

questions.question: In what year CE did the Great Heathen Army land in East Anglia to commence the conquest of England?
questions.explanation: The Great Heathen Army arrived in 865 CE, systematically invading Northumbria, Mercia, and East Anglia.

questions.question: What type of distinctive Viking sword featured a double-edged pattern-welded blade and an inlaid iron maker mark like Ulfberht?
questions.explanation: Ulfberht swords were crafted from crucible crucible steel with high carbon content, providing unmatched flexibility and sharpness.

questions.question: Which King of England famously halted the Viking advance and negotiated peace at the Treaty of Wedmore in 878 CE?
questions.explanation: Alfred the Great of Wessex defended his kingdom, fortified burhs, and encouraged literacy and naval defense against Danish forces.

questions.question: What were the carved runic stones erected in Jelling, Denmark, honoring King Gorm and Harald Bluetooth called?
questions.explanation: The Jelling Stones are recognized as Denmark birth certificate, commemorating Harald Christianization of the Danes.

questions.question: What alcoholic beverage brewed from fermented honey and water was central to Norse feasts and hospitality?
questions.explanation: Mead was celebrated in Norse poetry, most famously in the myth of the Mead of Poetry crafted from the blood of Kvasir.

questions.question: What was the title of the Norse law-speaker who memorized and recited the entire legal code at the annual Althing?
questions.explanation: The Logsogumadr (law-speaker) was elected for a three-year term to recite one-third of the Commonwealth law each summer.

questions.question: Approximately how many runic characters made up the standard Scandinavian Younger Futhark alphabet?
questions.explanation: Unlike the earlier 24-character Elder Futhark, the Viking Age Younger Futhark was streamlined to exactly 16 letters.

questions.question: Which Scandinavian court poet composed complex alliterative verses celebrating royal victories and heritage?
questions.explanation: Skalds employed intricate poetic meters like drottkvaett and colorful metaphorical kennings to compose oral histories.

questions.question: Which large Swedish island in the Baltic Sea served as a premier Viking trading nexus with massive silver deposits?
questions.explanation: Gotland has yielded more Viking Age silver coins and hoards than any other geographic area in Scandinavia.

questions.question: What type of timber church with wooden corner posts and dragon head ridges was built across medieval Norway?
questions.explanation: Stave churches like Urnes and Borgund combined Christian cruciform architecture with traditional Viking woodworking motifs.

questions.question: Which legendary Norse hero used the sword Gram to slay the dragon Fafnir and claim the cursed golden treasure hoard?
questions.explanation: Sigurd (Siegfried) the Volsung slew Fafnir, tasted dragon blood to understand birds, and won the Rhine gold.

questions.question: What protective textile material was boiled and pressed to make waterproof clothing for Viking sailors on ocean voyages?
questions.explanation: Dense wool saturated with natural sheep lanolin oils provided warmth and water repellency in harsh North Atlantic gales.

questions.question: In what year CE was the historic Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte signed, granting Normandy to Rollo?
questions.explanation: Signed in 911 CE, this treaty created the Duchy of Normandy to serve as a defensive buffer against other Viking raiders.

questions.question: What Norse explorer was the father of Leif Erikson and established the first permanent Norse colonies on Greenland?
questions.explanation: Erik Thorvaldsson (Erik the Red) was exiled from Iceland and founded the Eastern and Western Settlements in Greenland in 985 CE.

questions.question: Which major Viking trading town in southern Denmark near modern Schleswig controlled trade between the North and Baltic seas?
questions.explanation: Hedeby was protected by the Danevirke earthworks and was the largest Scandinavian urban market in the Viking Age.

questions.question: What is the rainbow bridge connecting Midgard (Earth) with Asgard (realm of the gods) guarded by Heimdall?
questions.explanation: Bifrost is the shimmering burning rainbow bridge guarded by the watchman god Heimdall with his horn Gjallarhorn.

questions.question: Which King of Norway was canonized as a Christian saint and patron of Norway after dying at the Battle of Stiklestad in 1030?
questions.explanation: King Olaf II (Saint Olaf) completed the Christianization of Norway and his shrine at Nidaros Cathedral became a major pilgrimage center.

questions.question: What round wooden defensive weapon did Viking warriors interlock to create an impenetrable shield wall (skjaldborg)?
questions.explanation: Viking round shields of linden wood were rimmed with leather and fitted with a central iron boss to deflect strikes.

questions.question: In what year CE did King Olaf Haraldsson die at the Battle of Stiklestad before being canonized as Saint Olaf?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Stiklestad occurred on July 29, 1030 CE, solidifying Christianity as the state religion in Norway.

questions.question: What Norse game of strategy, similar to chess, pitted a central king and defenders against a larger attacking force?
questions.explanation: Hnefatafl (King Table) was an asymmetrical board game played widely across Northern Europe throughout the Viking Age.

questions.question: Which Swedish island town on Lake Malaren was a pivotal trading hub visited by Saint Ansgar in the 9th century?
questions.explanation: Birka was an international emporium where merchants exchanged furs, amber, glass beads, and Byzantine silks.

questions.question: What was the compensation money paid by a killer to the family of a victim under Germanic and Norse law to prevent blood feuds?
questions.explanation: Weregild (man-price) established a monetary valuation on individuals according to their social status to settle homicides.

questions.question: Which son of Ragnar Lothbrok acquired a legendary moniker due to a physical affliction or tactical cunning?
questions.explanation: Ivar the Boneless was a primary commander of the Great Heathen Army and conquered York in 866 CE.

questions.question: What Norse term designated the tax or tribute demanded by Viking fleets to spare English towns from destruction?
questions.explanation: English kings such as Aethelred the Unready paid hundreds of thousands of pounds of silver in Danegeld to buy off raiding armies.

questions.question: In approximately what year CE was the settlement of Vinland in North America established by Norse explorers?
questions.explanation: Norse sagas and radiocarbon dating at L'Anse aux Meadows place the Vinland exploration around 1000 CE.

questions.question: What was the Norse name for the city of York after it was captured and colonized by Vikings in 866 CE?
questions.explanation: Jorvik became a thriving industrial and trading metropolis under Scandinavian rule for nearly a century.

questions.question: Which Norse god sacrificed one of his eyes at the Well of Mimir to gain supreme cosmic wisdom?
questions.explanation: Odin gave his right eye to drink from the waters of Mimir well and hung for nine days on Yggdrasil to master the runes.

questions.question: What metal was the most coveted medium of exchange in Viking commerce, frequently cut into hack-silver for small payments?
questions.explanation: Viking economy was based on bullion weight; silver ingots and jewelry were cut into fragments (hack-silver) to match scale balances.

questions.question: Which Norse god of justice sacrificed his right hand to the jaws of the monstrous wolf Fenrir?
questions.explanation: Tyr placed his hand in Fenrir mouth as a pledge of good faith while the other gods bound the wolf with Gleipnir.

questions.question: What is the oldest continuously published collection of Old Norse sagas and mythological poems written in 13th-century Iceland?
questions.explanation: The Poetic Edda preserved ancient alliterative poems like the Voluspa and Havamal, recording foundational Norse myth.

questions.question: Approximately how many metric tons of silver did King Aethelred the Unready pay in total Danegeld during Viking raids on England?
questions.explanation: Historical records chronicle over 150,000 pounds (approx. 60-70 metric tons) of silver paid in Danegeld between 991 and 1014 CE.
